speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, and how long has it been present? Does it itch, burn, or feel painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash involve the face, neck, or diaper area, and is there a history of eczema or asthma in the family? Are there any signs of secondary infection, such as oozing or crusting?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presentation of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead in an infant is classic for seborrheic dermatitis, often referred to as cradle cap. I will confirm this clinical diagnosis and rule out other possibilities. DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic dermatitis
